overview: Raymond was one of the senior princes of the First Crusade and a powerful lord from southern France. He helped lead the expedition through Antioch and toward Jerusalem, while his ambitions later centered on Tripoli.
Raymond is remembered as a devout but ambitious crusade prince whose career shows how pilgrimage, territorial lordship, and noble competition intertwined.

contentSections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Raymond was one of the senior princes of the First Crusade and a powerful lord from southern France. He helped lead the expedition through Antioch and toward Jerusalem, while his ambitions later centered on Tripoli.

contentSections.title: Birth and early life
paragraphs: Raymond came from the comital house of Toulouse and ruled one of the richest principalities in southern France. His age, status, and resources made him one of the most senior lay leaders to answer Urban II.

contentSections.title: Character and Personality
paragraphs: Raymond IV of Toulouse is remembered as the proud, wealthy, and difficult elder statesman of the First Crusade, a leader whose ambition and prickliness repeatedly set him at odds with his fellow princes. The sources present the oldest and richest of the crusade's commanders, deeply pious and close to the papal legate Adhemar, yet so conscious of his own status that his rivalries — especially with Bohemond of Antioch — hampered the leadership at crucial moments.

He was associated with the controversy over the Holy Lance at Antioch, which his own followers had discovered and which his rivals doubted, and his ambitions for a princely territory of his own were frustrated more than once. The chroniclers present him as devout and serious but also stubborn, jealous of precedence, and not always able to subordinate his pride to the common cause.

What the record supports is a powerful, religiously committed, but contentious leader whose age and wealth gave him standing he could not always convert into authority. He is remembered as the grand, quarrelsome senior of the crusade — pious and formidable, yet undone in his ambitions by the rivalries his own pride helped sustain.

contentSections.title: As count and crusader prince
paragraphs: Raymond’s leadership was marked by piety, wealth, and rivalry with other crusade princes, especially Bohemond over Antioch. He refused to accept a subordinate role and later pursued power around Tripoli.

contentSections.title: Death
paragraphs: Raymond died in 1105 during the long effort to establish a Latin lordship at Tripoli. His followers continued the project that became the County of Tripoli.

timeline.title: Born in southern France
timeline.description: Raymond was born into the ruling house of Toulouse, giving him wealth and status before the crusade.

timeline.title: Joins the First Crusade
timeline.description: He departed with one of the largest contingents from southern France.

timeline.title: Disputes Antioch
timeline.description: Raymond clashed with Bohemond over the future of Antioch after its capture.

timeline.title: Reaches Jerusalem
timeline.description: He took part in the campaign that ended with the capture of Jerusalem.

timeline.title: Dies near Tripoli
timeline.description: Raymond died while pursuing a new Latin principality on the Syrian coast.
